source.title: The Word Tariff
source.summary: How the Arabic ta'rif, meaning "to make known," became the most debated word in modern trade policy.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: In February 2025, the word "tariff" appeared in 847 news headlines in a single week. But where did this word come from? Travel back to 10th-century Alexandria, where transparent customs schedules called ta'rif revolutionized Mediterranean trade. Meet the Karimi merchants who built multinational trade networks, and discover how a word born from trade freedom became the vocabulary of trade protection.

x.single_post: Most people think tariffs are about protecting domestic industry. They are actually about making trade predictable. The Arabic ta'rif meant "to make known" — transparent customs schedules that let Mediterranean merchants calculate costs in advance.

linkedin.post: The word "tariff" dominated headlines this February, appearing 847 times in a single week. But this contentious term has surprising origins. It comes from the Arabic ta'rif, meaning "to make known" — referring to transparent customs schedules in 10th-century Alexandria that revolutionized Mediterranean trade. These schedules allowed merchants to calculate costs in advance, making trade predictable rather than arbitrary. The Karimi merchants leveraged this transparency to build multinational trade networks spanning from Egypt to India. What began as a tool for trade freedom eventually became the vocabulary of trade restriction. Language carries the memory of economic systems we've forgotten. Sometimes the etymology reveals more than the policy debates. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-tt-1
